topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
transcript:
[00:00] Ava Chen: All right thanks everyone for joining, this is Ava from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account. Marco Ruiz from infra will join on the technical bits. quick intro?
[00:06] Priya Nair: Hi, Priya here, Head of AI at Northshore. Liam and Renee are with me. We're exploring options to add generative product search and assistant features.
[00:12] Marco Ruiz: Hey all, Marco. We'll jump into perf and hosting later.
[00:18] Liam O'Sullivan: Morning. we're mostly on GCP, some on-prem for sensitive datasets.
[00:22] Ava Chen: Great, thanks. high level agenda: quickstart path and credits, then hosting options (hosted, dedicated, private), and security checks. we'll try to surface time-to-first-token and what a pilot looks like. sound good?
[00:34] Priya: Yup, sounds good. our main constraints: data residency in us-east for PII subsets, SOC2 required, low latency for product search (p95 ~ 150ms if possible), and cost target roughly to keep inference spend under current search infra baseline.
[00:48] Ava: Excellent, that's helpful. quick question on throughput — bursts versus steady state?
[00:52] Priya: Mostly steady with big bursts during sales windows. expected 50 to 300 qps depending on SKU.
[00:58] Marco: okay so that's a good range. on Hosted we can do autoscaling and routing but if you want isolation and guaranteed throughput Dedicated is the safer bet. Private gives full network control but more setup.
[01:12] Renee Zhang: Security — we need SSO (SAML/Okta), KMS integration for keys, audit logs, and ideally that private deployment for regulated SKUs. But for initial pilot we might be open to hosted if data is tokenized.
[01:28] Ava: Totally. our PLG/self-serve route typically gets teams to first token in under an hour — SDKs, curl examples, quickstart app and free pilot credits. we usually provide a playground and sample prompts for product search.
[01:40] Omar Delgado: When you say "first token in under an hour" what are the typical steps?
[01:44] Marco: Signup, create API key, run the sample request, check tokens in console, we have a hosted model catalog — most customers hit it in 20-45 minutes. network/vpc setup not needed for hosted.
[01:55] Priya: Good. cost — any guidance on token economics?
[01:58] Ava: We'll share our cost sheet. for pilot we can provision credits so you can run benchmarks. generation vs embeddings cost differs; for retrieval-augmented search you can optimize by shorter contexts and caching.
[02:12] Priya: For latency p95 of 150ms, is that realistic on hosted?
[02:16] Marco: depends on model and sequence length. small/optimized reranker models on hosted with our low-latency nodes can hit p95 ~ 80-150ms for short requests; larger models will be higher. Dedicated gives tighter SLOs. another lever is quantization + KV cache.
[02:34] Liam: Are there network hops to consider with hosted? we are in us-east, so region match should help.
[02:39] Marco: yes we route by region. also you can configure smart routing and fallback to cheaper variants if capacity constrained.
[02:47] Renee: For security review, can you share SOC2 + pen test summaries and the architecture for Private (air-gapped option)?
[02:53] Ava: absolutely. we'll link SOC2 and our security pack. for Private we've got a deployment package and network diagrams; it's a few-week lead time typically.
[03:02] Priya: If we do Dedicated, what's the procurement look like?
[03:06] Ava: Dedicated is usually committed capacity monthly/annual contract. we can start with a small reserved pool and autoscaling policies. pricing and SLA details we'll include in the follow-up.
[03:16] Omar: Any story around model upgrades and rollouts? we need canary and easy rollback for production.
[03:21] Marco: yes rollouts are supported — canary, A/B, automatic fallback. you can pin model versions and use traffic splitting.
[03:28] Priya: For the pilot, we want to run a 2-week perf test with our query set, measure p95 and relevance metrics. can you host that and run benchmarks?
[03:36] Marco: we can. we'll give you example harness and can run a medium-run in our infra or you can run it client-side with the SDK. we'll also provide a benchmark spreadsheet.
[03:45] Ava: sounds like an action plan: we'll give $5k in pilot credits, quickstart guide, and schedule a technical deep dive where Marco walks infra through network and perf tuning.
[03:54] Liam: Ok. curious about eviction/caching — our product search does heavy prefix reuse. how do you handle KV cache or prefix caching?
[04:01] Marco: we have prefix/KV cache features and automatic caching heuristics; you can also persist KV cache between requests for sessions to save compute. that helps latency and cost.
[04:12] Priya: Onboarding flow — can our engineers self-serve while security signs off in parallel?
[04:16] Ava: yes, PLG flow supports self-serve usage under credits while security engages for Dedicated/Private evaluation. that's common.
[04:23] Renee: We will need to see RBAC controls and audit trail detail. also, integration with our internal KMS (Cloud KMS) is a must.
[04:32] Marco: we support KMS integrations and provide audit logs with token-level detail in Console.
[04:38] Omar: Any known gotchas for GCP customers?
[04:42] Marco: just region matching and egress. if you want Private, there's some networking config but we help with a runbook.
[04:47] Priya: How long to get Dedicated up and running?
[04:50] Ava: usually 2-4 weeks after contract depending on capacity and networking. Private can be 4-8 weeks. Hosted is immediate.
[04:57] Priya: Ok great. also curious about model catalog — do you have reranker templates?
[05:01] Marco: yes we have curated reranker and small embedding models; we'll recommend based on your QA set.
[05:09] Ava: we'll follow up with the quickstart repo link, the benchmark sheet, and security docs. recommend next step: technical deep dive next Tuesday with Liam/Renee and Marco.
[05:20] Priya: works for us. thanks everyone.
[05:23] Ava: thanks folks, we'll send notes and next steps.
[05:27] [call ends]
